column1: # Curated common-core packages — the single source of truth for the
# cross-platform toolset. The per-platform installers in opt/bin read this file
# so every machine gets the same core regardless of OS.
# Format: two whitespace-separated columns.  BREW  APT
#   * Use "-" when a package does not apply / isn't available for that manager.
#   * Lines starting with '#' and blank lines are ignored.
#   * Names only — no versions; pin elsewhere if you need a specific version.
# gh: pkg-install-apt adds GitHub CLI's official apt repo (via
# setup_gh_apt_repo.sh) first, so this resolves to the latest upstream release
# instead of the stale one in Ubuntu's universe. macOS gets a current gh via brew.
# yq: brew ships the mikefarah build; the apt `yq` is the unrelated kislyuk
# Python wrapper (incompatible syntax), so Linux/WSL gets yq from
# opt/scripts/system/install_yq.sh instead — hence the `-` in the APT column.
# zsh: install.sh sets it as the default login shell (chsh) when present.
# GNU userland on macOS (already present in the base Linux install)
# Linux build/runtime basics (provided by the Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS)
# Nerd Font (gsl) prerequisites. install.sh's font step
# + curl; installing them here guarantees they exist BEFORE that step runs. macOS
# ships all three and uses its own font path, so the BREW column is '-'.
# Kubernetes toolchain. apt has no kind package at all, and kubectl/helm need
# third-party apt repos that lag upstream — so Linux/WSL gets the official
# install.sh), hence the '-' APT column. macOS installs all three via brew.
